description:
Jumping spiders are insects that have compact black bodies with relatively short legs and can range in size from about 4-18 mm in length. Jumping spiders are typically covered in dense hairs or scales that are brightly colored or iridescent and their front legs are usually thicker and somewhat longer than their other legs. They are usually slow moving, but their agile jumps allow them to be good hunters and they live in a variety of habitats such as tropical areas or scrub lands. The male jumping spider usually performs complex courtship displays in which he bobs his body and waves his front legs in a highly specific manner in order to attract a mate.

Spidey Snack
I ran across a cute tan jumping spider.  He was taking a little trip while carrying a snack with him.  He was on one of the sandstone columns on the walking path above the spillway. 
Photo 2:
Orange Mustache
Male tan jumping spiders have an orange mustache and females have a white one.  He is looking at me now.  Most jumping spiders are very curious and will stare at people and sometimes jump on your finger if you offer it.  They won't bite unless you are rough with them.  
Photo 3:
ID Shot
After satisfying his curiosity about me, he turned and continued up the column.  I kept this shot to show more of the markings on his back.  It also was the best shot of his snack which is a little midge.  Doesn't everyone carry snacks when they go on a hike at the lake?

description:
Visual Description: This Tan Jumping Spider was approximately 0.5 inches in length with eight legs. The color of the body and legs were mostly tan or light brown and mottled with black markings throughout. The back had a chevron light-colored pattern. The spider was furry.

Defining Characteristics: Tan Jumping Spiders have varying shades of brown on their body and are furry. They also have a characteristic lighter-colored chevron pattern on their back. They can jump far as a means of defense and to catch prey. Eight eyes can also be seen that wraps all the way around their head. Spiders have two chelicerae and eight legs, which are a defining characteristc in the class Arachnida.

Habitat: This spider was found on a vertical wood post on a ramp in a marshy region at Lettuce Lake Park. They are able to blend in with their surroundings with their brown shades. Tan Jumping Spiders are usually found in the eastern regions of the United States on fences, trees, under the bark of trees, or a vertical surface.

Reference: Spider ID. URL: https://spiderid.com/locations/united-states/florida/

description:
This type of organism is small with its size range falling between 8.5 and 13mm in body length. Females are typically larger. The body of this organism is hairy and appears to be vertically shaped with the bottom half of it being both longer and wider than the upper half. Eight legs extend outwards from the body. The hairy body consists of several shades of brown and exhibits a wavy pattern. This organism is a protostome, a group of animals, so it features a blastopore that develops into a mouth and an opposite cavity that develops into the anus. It is also an invertebrate.   This organism was found in Lettuce Lake Park which is a freshwater environment. This species is found in the eastern United States, mostly on vertical surfaces such as tree trunks, fence posts, and walls. They also can be found living on and under the peeling bark of shagbark hickories. This type of spider and its eggs are a source of food for many predators such as birds, mammals, birds, wasps, and reptiles. This species does not possess a lot of defense mechanisms. However, their jumping ability, hence the name Tan jumping spiders, allows them to be able to make a quick getaway from predators. Their primary source of food consists of insects and other spiders to eat. They have impeccable vision and can communicate using movement. These species play a role in controlling insect populations.
